ci.tip.composition.body: Use {W}’s “{wt}” to structure your picture, then add {E}’s “{et}”, applied to an everyday Hong Kong scene of your own. Draw 3 thumbnail sketches to compare first.
ci.tip.composition.alt: Compare how {W} and {E} arrange the subject and space, then pick one compositional approach and draw 3 thumbnail sketches.
ci.tip.concept.body: Start from “{theme}” and choose a real experience from your own life (e.g. home, the journey to school, your neighbourhood). {E} explores “{eTag}” and {W} explores “{wTag}” — how would you tell your own version?
ci.tip.medium.body: Do a materials test: try “{wt2}” and “{et2}”, record the effects and how they feel{medium}, and add it to your SBA process record.
ci.tip.medium.alt: Try the same composition in two different media, record the effects and add them to your SBA process record.
ci.tip.reflection.body: In your SBA, state clearly what you borrowed from {E} / {W} (composition, concept or technique), what you changed, and why it suits your theme. Avoid directly imitating their style or best-known works.
